Live from NPR News, I'm Lakshmi Singh.
President Trump's known for renaming a gulf and a lake.
Now he wants to rename AI.
Today he said he wanted to drop the word artificial and rebrand it as super intelligence because
he says the other word makes the technology sound fake.
Trump was flanked by billionaire AI rivals who in recent weeks took opposing views on
whether AI needs to tighter regulation.
Trump says no to that and to calls to restrict construction of data centers.
There are so many people that want data centers, you know, the areas with data centers that

But heading into the midterm elections, recent national polls suggest heavy voter opposition

Gregory Allen, founder of the Independent Decision Tree Research, says it's the worst

It is very bad at monitorability and it's also bad at alignment.
And those are exactly the kinds of things that now after the hugging face incident,
OpenAI is unwilling to release into the open public.
However smart this model is, it's just not safe yet.
Allen on NPR is here now.
Former Justice Department Special Counsel Jack Smith was on Capitol Hill today testifying
before lawmakers Smith defended his investigations of President Trump and said he would not be
intimidated by threats of prosecution.
Here's NPR's Ryan Lucas.
In his appearance before the Senate Judiciary Committee, Jack Smith said he stands by his
decision to bring charges against President Trump and that politics played no role in
the investigation.
The charges against President Trump were the result of the evidence.
Evidence of election interference, obstruction and the mishandling of classified documents.
Republicans repeatedly went after Smith, accusing him of conducting a partisan investigation
to get Trump and Republicans more broadly.
Some echoed Trump's calls for Smith himself to be prosecuted, to which Smith replied,
I will not be silenced by continued threats of prosecution from the president or others.
The more than four hour hearing ended where it began with a bitter partisan divide.
Ryan Lucas, NPR News, Washington.
Consumer confidence in the U.S. economy is the lowest it has been in more than 10 years.
Dana Peterson, the chief economist of the conference board that released the survey
today says the consumer confidence index deteriorated notably in September following two prior months
of softening.
U.S. stocks end the day low with a Dow down 131 points.
It's NPR News.
The food delivery drivers shot during an immigration enforcement action in Austin, Texas earlier
this month has been charged with assaulting a federal officer.
Moos Bichel of Member Station KUT has more.
In early accounts from his legal team, Wilbur Garces Perez said he did not know he was being
pursued by immigration agents before he was shot.
But a criminal complaint filed by ICE says officers identified themselves during an initial
stop before he fled in his car, hitting one of them with a side view mirror.
That led to a chase and ended with one agent forcing a stop, then shooting Garces Perez,
saying he feared he'd be struck by the car.
The criminal complaint says one of the two officers was wearing a body camera for the
initial stop, but that the agent turned the camera off before arriving at the scene of
the shooting.
Garces Perez has filed a federal lawsuit, primarily seeking to block deportation.
I'm Moos Bichel in Austin.
The U.S. Department of Education has extended the enrollment period for student loan borrowers
to lower their interest rates more from NPR's Sequoia Carillo.
Nearly two million federal student loan borrowers have already enrolled in auto pay and reduced
their interest rate for the next two years.
The initiative, announced by the Department of Education this summer, aims to get more
borrowers back to regular repayment after the COVID-19 payment freeze.
The department said borrower participation in auto pay dropped from 83 percent in 2019
to just 40 percent in 2025.
Borrowers now have until the end of the calendar year, December 31, to enroll in auto pay.
Those already enrolled in the program do not need to take any action to receive the benefit.
That's Sequoia Carillo.
